title: 第二十五章 明镜高悬光明正大第二十六章 明心见性击鼓鸣冤
content_zh:
“怪不得，怪不得！”庆丰一副恍然大悟的表情。
“怪不得翠红那小妮子，使了劲的给我灌酒，初时我还以为她是想多卖点酒，挣点盈利。
如今看来.....分明就是想灌醉我！”
铁棠将现有线索串联起来，暗自思量。
看来翠红显然也是知情人士，所以她才会被吴青灭口。
这应当也是吴青意料之外的事，所以才会显得如此仓促，甚至在现场留下许多铁证。
他后面应该还有人！
对比干脆利落的马场无头案来说，怡红院案子的线索、证据，都太多，太明显了。
不知是同伙，还是幕后指使？
亦或二者皆有？
庆丰喝得酩酊大醉，除了成为替罪羊之外，还丢了一把刀和自身腰牌。
可一个从九品官员的腰牌.....又能掀起什么风浪？
笃！笃！
牢房外传来叩门声，打断了铁棠思绪。
“又有何事？”他的语气有些恼怒，总感觉每次审问庆丰，都不是太过顺畅。
袁骅小声说道：“头，庆丰的婆娘来了。”
“来了就来了，让她一边待着，莫非还要我给她让位不成？”铁棠连庆丰都不放在眼里，哪里会管他家的娘子。
“咳，头，这次不同的，不同的，她不是孤身前来，听说还有清水郡的大人物相伴。”
铁棠一皱眉，还是断然拒绝：“让她等着！”
“啊...头，知县也在那边陪同呢。”

“呵！”
“有意思。”
..........
县衙，三省堂。
三省堂，取自《吾日三省吾身》之意，是知县正常办公议政、会客迎宾之所。
也有一些涉及机密、隐私、不宜公开的案件在这审理。
门前除了高悬的黑底黄字匾额，左右还分别挂有楹联。
上联书：‘吃百姓之饭，穿百姓之衣，莫道百姓可欺。’
下联写：‘得一官不荣，失一官不辱，勿说一官无用。’
词藻并不华丽，语言质朴，却寓意深刻。
铁棠移步至此，认真看了几眼楹联，才晃晃悠悠地走了进去。
这里他来得也不多，没怎么好好看过。
堂内正中悬挂着‘清慎勤’三个大字的牌匾，下方正首端坐着身披官袍的知县。
在他下方左侧，则是坐着两位铁棠不认识的人，一男一女。
男的约莫五六十上下，女的看起来只有三十，二者皆显福态，着锦穿罗。
他们双手、脖颈之间穿金戴银，折射的光芒微微有些晃眼，在身后还站着四五位仆役，同样衣着光鲜，神气自得。
“铁棠拜见县令大人！”
content_en:
"No wonder, no wonder!" Qingfeng said with an expression of sudden realization.
"No wonder that little girl Cuihong tried her best to drink me wine. At first, I thought she wanted to sell more wine and make some profit.
Now it seems...it's clear that he wants to get me drunk! "
Tie Tang connected the existing clues and thought to himself.
It seems that Cuihong is also an insider, so she was silenced by Wu Qing.
This should be something Wu Qing didn't expect, that's why he seemed so hasty and even left a lot of irrefutable evidence at the scene.
There should be someone behind him!
Compared to the neat and simple Headless Case in the Racecourse, the clues and evidence in the Yihongyuan case are too many and too obvious.
I wonder if he is an accomplice or the instigator?
Or maybe both?
Qingfeng was so drunk that in addition to becoming a scapegoat, he also lost a knife and his own badge.
But what kind of trouble could a ninth-rank official create?
Benedict! Benedict!
A knock on the door came from outside the cell, interrupting Tie Tang's thoughts.
"What's the matter?" His tone was a little angry. He always felt that every time he interrogated Qingfeng, it was not smooth.
Yuan Hua whispered: "Boss, Qingfeng's mother-in-law is here."
"Come here as soon as you come, let her stay alone, do you want me to make way for her?" Tie Tang didn't even take Qingfeng seriously, so how could he care about his wife.
"Ahem, head, it's different this time, different. She didn't come alone. I heard she was accompanied by a big shot from Qingshui County."
Tie Tang frowned, but still flatly refused: "Let her wait!"
"Ah...head, the magistrate is accompanying you there too."
"Ha!"
"Interesting."
...........
County government, three provinces hall.
Sanshengtang, taken from the meaning of "I will examine my body three times in a day", is the place where the county magistrate normally conducts business and discusses affairs, receives guests and welcomes guests.
There are also cases that involve confidentiality, privacy, and are not suitable for public disclosure.
In addition to the black plaque with yellow characters hanging high in front of the door, there are also couplets hanging on the left and right.
The first couplet reads: "Eat the food of the people, wear the clothes of the people, and never think that the people can be bullied." ’
The second couplet reads: "It is no honor to gain an official position; it is no disgrace to lose an official official position; do not say that an official official position is useless." ’
The vocabulary is not gorgeous, the language is simple, but the meaning is profound.
Tie Tang moved here, looked at the couplets carefully for a few times, and then walked in unsteadily.
He didn't come here much, so he didn't take a good look at it.
In the middle of the hall hangs a plaque with the three characters "Qing Shen Qin", and directly below sits the magistrate in official robes.
Below him, on the left side, were two people Tie Tang didn't recognize, a man and a woman.
The man is about fifty or sixty, and the woman looks to be only thirty. Both of them look blessed, wearing brocade and robes.
They wore gold and silver between their hands and necks, and the reflected light was slightly dazzling. Behind them stood four or five servants, equally well-dressed and proud.
"Tie Tang pays homage to the county magistrate!"
